gen-gf-tektur-gf-nobile: Tektur has outsized lowercase and bent-wire curves that never pinch or flare at the ends. Nobile follows with a low, compact build, its open letter mouths giving the text a contemporary steadiness the heading deliberately skips.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-nokora: Wire-bent and unmistakable, Tektur keeps its s curves full right through the spine. Nokora then lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase, and its wide s never tightens, so the sans feels sturdy where the heading feels showy.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Noto Kufi Arabic reads modern and unfussy, with a welcoming gap in the c and capitals barely above the lowercase. Yet Tektur matches it with diagonals that echo its stems, and that shared geometry is what ties the two together.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans: Noto Sans reads smoothly, its lowercase bodies filling most of the letter height and its c opening wide. Yet Tektur is the one to show off, built from a single stroke width, while the sans simply carries the text.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Expressive, with glyphs that look cut from strips of equal width. Tektur grabs attention up top, while the plain sans of Noto Sans Adlam keeps its curve endings well apart and its c, s and z tall and full.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unjoine: Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined has generous space between curve ends and stems, and little height difference between its cases. Yet the strongest quality here is Tektur's rounded-nib look, with no swelling at the stroke ends, set against that restraint.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hie: Rounded strokes like cut lengths of cord make Tektur instantly recognizable. It is built to stand out, and Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs is built to recede, with outward-pointing terminals and an x-height rising close to cap height.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Clean and modern, Noto Sans Arabic opens wide on its small letters and carries a pronounced x-height. But shrink Tektur, with its one stroke thickness everywhere, and its distinctive looks begin to fade.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Noto Sans Armenian reads approachably, its c, s and z standing tall and full with wide, inviting round letters. Noto Sans Armenian would carry a long passage without tiring, while Tektur's signage-like plainness stays up in the heading.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Pipe-cleaner strokes, no hairlines, instant attitude. Noto Sans Balinese brings a breathing space inside every curved glyph and short ascenders, and that quiet restraint is the pair's real strength against Tektur's stems.
